newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares drop, lack of investors.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares drop, lack of investors.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange dropped in a market abandoned by major investors, with many liquidating ahead of telephone company CANTV's upcoming global share offering, traders said.
The market's 19-share index .IBC closed down 2.00 percent at 5,888.05 points. A total of 34 shares fell, five rose and three closed flat.
Just under 24 million shares traded worth five billion bolivars ($10.7 million).

More than half of those shares were Corimon B, which lost 15.79 percent to close at 12.00 bolivars. The Venezuelan paints and packaging company returned to trading on Monday after an eight-month suspension.
The market lacked investors "because the Americans are looking at one thing, the U.S. presidential elections, and local ones wait for CANTV," said Jose Gregorio Tineo, of Multinvest brokerage.
The Venezuelan government outlined Thursday morning the global share offering of CANTV that will see 40 percent of the company's stock placed on local and international markets.
The share price is expected to be known on November 21, Venezuelan Investment Fund President Alberto Poletto said.
